entry.title: Messaging 1.35.55
entry.content:
# Messaging 1.35.55
- When you link Messaging to a Signal account whose main phone runs Signal's own app, Signal now offers to transfer your message history, and Messaging brings it in: the text of one-to-one and group chats, with replies, edits and read state. Photos and files from before the link show as not downloaded; reactions, stickers, polls and call notes are left out. A Signal Desktop export can still be brought in on top, without doubling anything - A linked phone can now become your Signal account's main device, with no text code: Settings → Signal → Signal account → Make main device. Safety numbers stay the same, and so does whether your number can find you. Whatever held the account before is signed out, whether a phone or a computer or server running Signal, along with every linked device, Signal Desktop included; if Signal says no, nothing changes

entry.title: Messaging 1.35.54
entry.content:
# Messaging 1.35.54
- Settings are regrouped so each setting sits where you would look for it: Archived, Scheduled and Blocking on their own at the top, then Notifications, Display, Sending, Privacy and security, Signal, Desktop Sync, Backup and sync, and Help. Nothing was added or taken away - The Signal settings page is grouped under headings (Account, Conversations, Privacy, Calls and background, Contacts, History, Network), with Delete Signal data last on its own - Every settings page now opens at its top, and a heading turns the page together with the rows under it - About two months after this version's Signal parts were last brought up to date, the Signal line in Settings says an update is due, so a new version can go on before Signal starts refusing the old one

entry.title: Messaging 1.35.53
entry.content:
# Messaging 1.35.53
- When Signal hands Messaging a copy of a message you sent from your main phone and Messaging cannot take it in at first, it now keeps the copy and tries again later, instead of losing it quietly. If it still cannot, a short note in that conversation says a message is missing - An edit, deletion or reaction that arrives before the message it belongs to now waits for it, so a deleted message stays deleted - When Messaging is your Signal account's own phone and Signal asks it to prove it is a person, tapping the Not sent line now opens that check right in Messaging; once it is answered, the held-up messages are sent again - A phone whose Signal registration was taken over is now told to register again, not to link

entry.title: Messaging 1.35.52
entry.content:
# Messaging 1.35.52
- Linking this phone to Signal follows Signal 8.37.3: the link code's encryption is now done by Signal's own library - A link code nobody scans now ends after about five minutes with a clear "nobody scanned the code in time", instead of waiting forever - The conversation list no longer shows random previews in italics: italics mark a draft and nothing else

entry.title: Messaging 1.35.51
entry.content:
# Messaging 1.35.51
- A Signal message that could not be sent stays in the conversation as "Not sent", with the reason and a tap to send it again - Switching Signal off now closes the composer at once, and switching it back on reconnects without restarting the app - A message too long for Signal is turned down straight away, not after half a minute - Receipts, the account's records and the sender certificate follow Signal's own timing more closely

entry.title: Topo 0.2.25
entry.content:
# Topo 0.2.25
- Plan one section of a path: on a point, choose "Section from here", then tap where the section ends. Topo shows its length, climb and descent, and draws it bolder on the map. "Follow section" leads to it and along the trail to its end, even when you are not on the path yet. - Tapping the path line on a path's map picks the nearest point, also when the path draws no points. - Descent no longer shows with a minus sign while following a path.
